  characters: Sumitra, Kausalya

  title: Kausalya lets Ram go
  characters: Kausalya, Ram, Lakshman
  opening: His mother had waited seventeen years for this day, and it was taken from her in a morning.
  summary: Ram's mother faints at the news and begs to come with him. Ram gently refuses, asks her to look after his grieving father, and wins her blessing for the journey.
  lesson: Love sometimes means staying behind to care for someone else.
- id: yv.p.punya_pavana
  title: Punya consoles his younger brother Pavana after their parents die
  characters: Punya, Pavana, Dirghatapas
  opening: When their parents died, one brother quietly lit the funeral fires and the other ran weeping into the forest.
  summary: Two brothers live with their parents by the Ganga. When their father and mother die, the elder, Punya, performs the rites calmly while the younger, Pavana, wanders the forest weeping. Punya gently helps him see that the bonds of 'mine' and 'not mine' are made in the mind. Vasishtha draws the lesson: worry grows when fed, and a full mind finds the world full.
  lesson: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.
- id: vr.p.father_one_more_night
  title: One more night: Ram leaves his father
  characters: Dasharatha, Ram
  opening: His father asked for only one thing: one more night.
  summary: The broken king begs Ram to stay one more night so his parents can see him. Ram gently refuses, saying a promise made must be kept and he will return in fourteen years. Dasharatha embraces him and collapses.
  lesson: Goodbyes to ageing parents are hard; leave with love and a promise to return.
- id: rcm.p.ram_kausalya
  title: Kausalya lets her son go
  characters: Kausalya, Ram, Sita
  opening: She had the sweets ready for his coronation when he came to say goodbye.
  summary: Ram comes to his mother as she is preparing for his coronation. Torn between duty and love, she decides not to hold him back with 'false affection', blesses him and asks only that he not forget her. As he leaves she wonders aloud whether she will live to see his face again.
  lesson: Letting a child go with your blessing is love at its hardest.
